source.title: Alignment-Aware Model Adaptation via Feedback-Guided Optimization
source.authors: Gaurav Bhatt; Aditya Chinchure; Jia-Wei Zhou; Leonid Sigal

page_placements.theme: Training recovery beyond the opening can improve robustness

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates harmful-response rates after adversarial fine-tuning and under prefilling attacks, but with its own training and evaluation setup rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports safety outcomes after fine-tuning and under prefilling, so those results are included. Claims about per-token KL concentration, localized safety parameters, why safety is shallow, and deepening safety are not measured. Statements in Related Work about other studies are citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper (AWARE). Its undefended baselines still measure the claimed behaviour. Plain PEFT on Alpaca or Bio-Instruct, with or without injected BeaverTails harmful data, gives high HEx-PHI harmful scores. Harmful-token prefilling raises harmful scores for the base model and for the DPO-C and LISA models. The setup is the study's own (5000 samples, LoRA, GPT-4o-mini judge), not a replication. No pre-fine-tuning harmful score is reported for the instruct models.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that AWARE's verifier-guided, adaptively gated fine-tuning reduces harmful and hallucinated outputs while preserving task performance. They also conclude that it corrects unsafe initializations and that learned creative abstention resists prefilling. Separately, they state that likelihood-only PEFT erodes pretrained safety.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 5000-sample instruction-tuning datasets with injected unsafe examples and an external verifier; evaluates harmful scores and a learned abstention defense rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The prefilling outcome differs by defense: AWARE with creative abstention is reported to be more robust than AWARE-D with default refusal templates. The harmful-data fraction also varies in the Alpaca experiment; the text says DPO-C worsens while AWARE remains stable.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO-C, Qi et al.'s token-weighted constrained fine-tuning objective, only partly limits harmful fine-tuning: HS 52.3 at ur=0.1 vs PEFT 92.5, and 68.3 at ur=0.4. It still degrades under prefilling and fails to recover safety from an unsafe initialization (Fig. 4c).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-token constrained fine-tuning objectives give only partial protection against harmful fine-tuning and prefilling.

fits_no_version.finding: Training learned, context-specific refusals (AWARE creative abstention) gives the lowest harmful score across prefill lengths; template refusals (AWARE-D) degrade faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on varied, context-aware refusals improves robustness to prefilling more than fixed refusal templates.

record.problems: Prefilling results are described in text but their numeric values are only in a figure. The text extraction does not permit reliable assignment of the flattened Table 2 values to individual unsafe ratios and methods. The benign-data result lacks a numeric before-versus-after safety comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many comparison methods and model/domain task-quality metrics. Rows for those non-PEFT methods in Table 7 were not included because the selected rows already capture the harmful-fine-tuning safety outcome; Table 2's flattened numeric entries were not assigned to individual conditions where their layout did not support a confident mapping.

untested.parts: The few-example regime: only 5000-sample mixes with ur 0.1 and 0.4 are tested, and no pre-fine-tuning baseline is given.
Carefully selected benign data is not tested. Only Llama-3.2-1B on Alpaca is run at ur=0.0, with no pre-fine-tuning baseline.
Suffix attacks and decoding changes are not tested; prefilling results are figure-only.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens is not tested. DPO-C (Qi et al.'s token-weighted constrained objective) appears only as a baseline; see fits_no_version.

missing.what: Plain PEFT HS on Llama-3.2-1B Alpaca across unsafe ratios: 71.5 at ur=0.0 (benign), 92.5 at ur=0.1, 96.5 at ur=0.4. This gives both the V2 benign value and a V1 dose-response.
Harmful score rises sharply over training under task-only SFT (Eq. 3).

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope label was removed: the few-example regime is untested, not shown to fail. The V4 limits_scope label was removed because it rested only on the study's own defense. Table 2 and Table 7 differ slightly for AWARE at ur=0.1 on Alpaca (34.3 vs 33.7). The prefilling base model and prefix lengths are not specified. No pre-fine-tuning harmful score is given for any instruct model, which weakens both V1 and V2 support.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning with only a few examples; the stated adversarial setup uses 5000 samples, with an unsafe fraction.
The benign-data comparison does not provide a numeric before-versus-after safety rate for the same checkpoint.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Suffix attacks and decoding changes are not evaluated.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training designed to spread safety beyond the first tokens and whether that protection persists.
